- Uses quantum interference (Hadamard gate on amplitude-encoded image) for edge/gradient detection
- Complexity O(1) vs O(N) classical on pre-encoded image
- Application: histopathology, general image filtering [Goyal et al.]
- Integration: Sequential (quantum-first)
- **IMPLEMENTED in TF-CLIP-quantum** with learnable alpha mixing weight

### QPIE — Quantum Probability Image Encoding
- Encodes pixel intensities as probability amplitudes in a quantum state
- Enables efficient quantum manipulation of image data
- No specific performance numbers in survey; mentioned as "powerful preprocessing filter" alongside QHED
- Integration: Sequential (quantum-first)
- **Not in TF-CLIP-quantum**

### Classical PCA → Quantum Input (dimensionality compression pipeline)
- Classical PCA or resizing first, then quantum encoding to match qubit count
- Ubiquitous in NISQ literature; known limitation: compression can lose discriminative info
- Integration: Sequential (classical-first)
- **Implicitly used** in all quantum stages via pre_net linear projection

**Why:** "quantum preprocessing" in this project = on raw images before ViT, not elsewhere. [[feedback-quantum-preprocessing]]

name: survey-feature-extraction
description: Quantum feature extraction techniques from survey paper — replaces or augments CNN/ViT feature learning
metadata:
  type: project
---

Source: "Toward Quantum-Enhanced Computer Vision" (Connor Druett et al.)

## Techniques

### Quanvolutional Neural Networks (QuNNs / Quanvolution)
- Quantum circuit acts as sliding local filter on image patches (analogous to conv kernel)
- Quantum pooling step reduces qubits via measurement-conditioned gates
- O(log N) parameters; passes feature maps to classical MLP/classifier head
- Results: +10% pneumonia [82], +10% COVID-19 severity (96.82%) [77], +3.2% breast cancer [57], +2.9% CIFAR-10 (parallel config) [85]
- Integration: Sequential, Parallel, Interlaced variants all exist
- **Partially in project**: QTemporal/TQA and QTD are temporal variants; no named quanvolutional layer

### Quantum Kernel / QSVM Feature Maps
- VQC encodes data points as quantum states; kernel k(a,b) = |⟨φ(a)|φ(b)⟩|²
- Variants: Z-feature map (no entanglement), ZZ-feature map (entangling), Pauli-X map
- Access to exponentially larger Hilbert spaces than classical kernels
- Results: 99.23% accuracy (ResNet + QSVM) [75], 94% pneumonia (Quanv+QSVM) [64]
- Integration: Sequential (classical backbone → QSVM)
- **Not in project** as standalone; QuantumSwapTest computes fidelity (related concept)

### Quantum Feature Selection via Quantum Annealing (QUBO)
- Frames feature selection as QUBO; quantum annealer (D-Wave) finds optimal feature subset
- Uses quantum tunneling to escape local minima in feature selection landscape
- Result: 86.89% accuracy, outperforming classical feature selection [96]
- Integration: Sequential (quantum feature selection → classical classifier)
- **Not in project**

### Quantum Autoencoder / Variational Autoencoder
- VQC trained as autoencoder; "untangles" representations into quantum probability vectors
- Classical softmax head interprets quantum feature vectors
- Avoids full quantum state readout complexity
- Integration: Sequential (quantum FE → classical classifier)
- **Not in project**

### Parallel Hybrid CNN + Quantum Convolution (PQCNN)
- Classical CNN branch + quantum convolution branch in parallel; outputs concatenated
- Classical: local features; quantum: global/non-linear correlations
- Key finding: quantum stream remained stable when classical stream failed under Gaussian noise [82]
- Result: improved accuracy over sequential-only models [91]
- Integration: Parallel
- **Not in project** (parallel pattern concept could apply)

### Q-C-Q Interlaced Feature Extractor
- Quantum FE → classical layer (dynamically parameterises second quantum circuit) → quantum classifier
- Captures complex visual info across two quantum stages with classical mediation
- Result: 95.18% MRI Brain Tumour (+5.7% over classical) [Long et al., 4-8 qubits]
- Integration: Interlaced (Q-C-Q sandwich)
- **Not in project** (QClassifierReupload was related but found intractable)

### Hybrid Quantum-Classical Transfer Learning (Dressed Quantum Circuit)
- Pretrained classical backbone (ResNet, VGG) → dimensionality reduction → VQC → classical head
- Backbone frozen; only VQC trained — direct analogue of classical transfer learning
- Results: 90% surface anomaly [8], 99.93% rice disease [3], 90.42% breast cancer [57], F1=0.76 trauma [32]
- CAUTION: Sünkel et al. [81] warn overly expressive classical pre/post layers overshadow quantum contribution
- Integration: Sequential (classical-first)
- **THIS IS THE CORE PATTERN of TF-CLIP-quantum** — CLIP backbone → quantum layers

**Note:** Multi-class degradation documented — VQC performance drops sharply with class count (1604-class AG-VPReID is hard). 768→8 compression is a known bottleneck (sequential architecture flaw). [[survey-classification]]

description: Quantum feature extraction techniques from survey paper — replaces or augments CNN/ViT feature learning
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 79b4d34a-c90e-4745-b162-fd7dca926d0b

Source: "Toward Quantum-Enhanced Computer Vision" (Connor Druett et al.)

## Techniques

### Quanvolutional Neural Networks (QuNNs / Quanvolution)
- Quantum circuit acts as sliding local filter on image patches (analogous to conv kernel)
- Quantum pooling step reduces qubits via measurement-conditioned gates
- O(log N) parameters; passes feature maps to classical MLP/classifier head
- Results: +10% pneumonia [82], +10% COVID-19 severity (96.82%) [77], +3.2% breast cancer [57], +2.9% CIFAR-10 (parallel config) [85]
- Integration: Sequential, Parallel, Interlaced variants all exist
- **Partially in project**: QTemporal/TQA and QTD are temporal variants; no named quanvolutional layer

### Quantum Kernel / QSVM Feature Maps
- VQC encodes data points as quantum states; kernel k(a,b) = |⟨φ(a)|φ(b)⟩|²
- Variants: Z-feature map (no entanglement), ZZ-feature map (entangling), Pauli-X map
- Access to exponentially larger Hilbert spaces than classical kernels
- Results: 99.23% accuracy (ResNet + QSVM) [75], 94% pneumonia (Quanv+QSVM) [64]
- Integration: Sequential (classical backbone → QSVM)
- **Not in project** as standalone; QuantumSwapTest computes fidelity (related concept)

### Quantum Feature Selection via Quantum Annealing (QUBO)
- Frames feature selection as QUBO; quantum annealer (D-Wave) finds optimal feature subset
- Uses quantum tunneling to escape local minima in feature selection landscape
- Result: 86.89% accuracy, outperforming classical feature selection [96]
- Integration: Sequential (quantum feature selection → classical classifier)
- **Not in project**

### Quantum Autoencoder / Variational Autoencoder
- VQC trained as autoencoder; "untangles" representations into quantum probability vectors
- Classical softmax head interprets quantum feature vectors
- Avoids full quantum state readout complexity
- Integration: Sequential (quantum FE → classical classifier)
- **Not in project**

### Parallel Hybrid CNN + Quantum Convolution (PQCNN)
- Classical CNN branch + quantum convolution branch in parallel; outputs concatenated
- Classical: local features; quantum: global/non-linear correlations
- Key finding: quantum stream remained stable when classical stream failed under Gaussian noise [82]
- Result: improved accuracy over sequential-only models [91]
- Integration: Parallel
- **Not in project** (parallel pattern concept could apply)

### Q-C-Q Interlaced Feature Extractor
- Quantum FE → classical layer (dynamically parameterises second quantum circuit) → quantum classifier
- Captures complex visual info across two quantum stages with classical mediation
- Result: 95.18% MRI Brain Tumour (+5.7% over classical) [Long et al., 4-8 qubits]
- Integration: Interlaced (Q-C-Q sandwich)
- **Not in project** (QClassifierReupload was related but found intractable)

### Hybrid Quantum-Classical Transfer Learning (Dressed Quantum Circuit)
- Pretrained classical backbone (ResNet, VGG) → dimensionality reduction → VQC → classical head
- Backbone frozen; only VQC trained — direct analogue of classical transfer learning
- Results: 90% surface anomaly [8], 99.93% rice disease [3], 90.42% breast cancer [57], F1=0.76 trauma [32]
- CAUTION: Sünkel et al. [81] warn overly expressive classical pre/post layers overshadow quantum contribution
- Integration: Sequential (classical-first)
- **THIS IS THE CORE PATTERN of TF-CLIP-quantum** — CLIP backbone → quantum layers

**Note:** Multi-class degradation documented — VQC performance drops sharply with class count (1604-class AG-VPReID is hard). 768→8 compression is a known bottleneck (sequential architecture flaw). [[survey-classification]]

---
name: survey-classification
description: Quantum classification techniques from survey paper — VQCs, SVMs, metric learning, re-uploading
metadata:
  type: project
---

Source: "Toward Quantum-Enhanced Computer Vision" (Connor Druett et al.)

## Techniques

### Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC / QNN Classifier)
- Parameterised circuit as classification head: encoding layer → variational ansatz U(θ) → Pauli-Z measurement → class labels
- Multi-class: multiple qubit measurements or parity encoding
- Results: 99.93% rice disease [3], 99.23% image classification [75], AUC 0.78 trauma [32]
- CRITICAL FINDING: ~90% binary MNIST → ~30% 10-class MNIST — severe multi-class scalability problem [Wu et al.]
- Integration: Sequential (classical backbone → VQC)
- **IMPLEMENTED** — QClassifier is the primary VQC classifier

### Quantum Support Vector Machine (QSVM)
- Quantum kernel matrix (fidelity between quantum-encoded pairs) → classical SVM dual solver
- Expressive decision boundaries in quantum Hilbert space; ZZ-feature map separates entangled classes
- Results: 99.23% [75], pneumonia [64]; ensemble with classical SVM via voting improves robustness [95]
- Integration: Sequential or Parallel ensemble
- **Not in project** directly; QuantumSwapTest computes related fidelity

### Quantum Metric Learning / Quantum Embeddings
- VQC projects data into quantum state space; inter-class distances via quantum state distance (e.g., swap test fidelity)
- Class boundaries from thresholded expectation values or state distances, not direct logits
- Suitable when class distributions are complex or overlapping [Lloyd et al. 47]
- Integration: Sequential or Interlaced
- **IMPLEMENTED** — QuantumSwapTest (fidelity-based similarity), QuantumTripletLoss (quantum kernel distances for metric learning), QGT (quantum-gated triplet)

### Data Re-uploading Classifier
- Repeatedly encodes classical input between processing layers in a single/few-qubit circuit
- Approximates complex non-linear functions without more qubits; higher expressivity than single-upload
- Result: enhanced image classification with genetic algorithm optimization [Mukhanbet & Daribayev 56]
- Noted in future directions for capturing complex visual info within qubit limits
- Integration: Interlaced (iterative classical-quantum loops)
- **IMPLEMENTED** — QClassifierReupload used this concept but found intractable on CPU (~57s/batch, 96-block), flagged for redesign [[project-reupload-redesign]]

### Quantum Federated Learning (QFL / QFNN)
- Distributes VQC training across multiple quantum devices; local training → central parameter aggregation
- Maintains data privacy; relevant for medical imaging
- Results: demonstrated for fraud detection and privacy-preserving classification [7, 31, 68]
- Integration: Distributed Sequential per node
- **Not in project**

### Quantum Clustering / Quantum K-Means
- Models dataset as aggregate wave function (Schrödinger's equation); cluster centres = potential field minima
- Handles non-convex cluster geometries; applicable to unsupervised segmentation and colour quantization
- Result: 99.6% accuracy, Dice > 0.85 for segmentation [Poggiali et al. 68]
- Integration: Sequential (standalone or post-processing classifier)
- **Not in project**

### Quantum Reinforcement Learning (QRL)
- VQC-based policy network; uses Differentiable Quantum Architecture Search (DQAS) to optimize circuit structure
- Mandatory bidirectional Q↔C loops every execution step; recursive refinement of re-upload maps
- Result: enhanced expressivity for resource-constrained scenarios [Sun et al. 80]
- Integration: Interlaced (mandatory iterative loop)
- **Not in project**

**Key finding from survey:** Multi-class degradation is a documented problem — performance degrades sharply with class count. Our 1604-class AG-VPReID setting is on the hard end. [[survey-feature-extraction]]

---
name: survey-optimisation
description: Quantum optimisation techniques from survey paper — training-time quantum optimizers and loss methods
metadata:
  type: project
---

Source: "Toward Quantum-Enhanced Computer Vision" (Connor Druett et al.)

## Techniques

### Quantum Annealing for Hyperparameter Optimization
- Maps hyperparameter search (LR, batch size, depth, filter counts) to Ising model ground-state search
- D-Wave annealer uses quantum tunneling to escape local minima in hyperparameter space
- Result: improved efficiency over classical grid/random search [García Amboage et al. 22]
- Integration: Sequential (quantum optimizer → classical model training)
- **Not in project**

### Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA)
- Variational quantum algorithm for combinatorial optimization (Ising/QUBO formulation)
- Alternating parameterised unitaries approximate optimal solutions; applicable to NAS, weight optimization, feature selection
- Mentioned alongside quantum annealing [22]; no specific CV accuracy numbers given in survey isolation
- Integration: Sequential (quantum optimizer → classical model)
- **Not in project**

### Grover's Search for Weight Optimization
- Frames weight search as unstructured database search; quadratic speedup O(√N) over classical search
- Reduces test loss; avoids local minima that trap backpropagation
- Results: reduced test loss, improved accuracy on small-scale datasets [Nigatu et al. 59, Du et al. 15]
- Limitation: currently limited to small networks due to qubit/gate complexity
- Integration: Sequential (quantum optimizer → classical network weights)
- **Not in project**

### Quantum Hypernetworks
- Quantum circuit generates weights for a classical neural network
- Combines architecture search + weight optimization in single quantum loop
- Accesses weight distributions not reachable by classical gradient methods
- Result: proposed via quantum annealing + tensor network simulations [Lami et al. 41]; limited CV results
- Integration: Interlaced (quantum generates weights → classical forward → quantum updated)
- **Not in project**

### Classical Optimizers for Quantum Circuits (Parameter-Shift, COBYLA, SPSA, Evolution Strategies)
- **Parameter-Shift Rule:** Exact quantum gradients via two shifted circuit evaluations; scales linearly (2 per param)
- **COBYLA:** Constrained optimization via linear approximations; fewer evaluations, more noise-robust
- **SPSA / Guided-SPSA:** Perturbs all parameters simultaneously; independent of parameter count, efficient for noisy high-dim spaces
- **Evolution Strategies:** Search-gradient-based; controls evaluation count, avoids gradient calculation
- Finding: COBYLA and SPSA more robust to NISQ noise than parameter-shift for deep circuits [Friedrich & Maziero 21, Periyasamy et al. 66]
- Integration: Applied within any hybrid architecture training loop
- **Implicitly in project** — PennyLane uses parameter-shift / backprop; `diff_method='backprop'` used throughout

### Differentiable Quantum Architecture Search (DQAS)
- Gradient-based automated design of quantum circuit ansatzes; reduces manual circuit design effort
- Finds optimal circuit structures for interlaced and QRL architectures
- Result: used for QRL by Sun et al. [80]; noted as future direction for reducing interlaced design complexity
- Integration: Interlaced (iterative search loop)
- **Not in project**

### Quantum Triplet Loss (QuantumTripletLoss) — project-specific
- Replaces Euclidean distance in triplet loss with trainable quantum kernel K(x_i, x_j) = cos(φ(x_i), φ(x_j))
- Distance d = 1 - K; VQC shape shapes feature space geometry at training time only; classical L2 at inference
- Circuit: pre_net (768→n_qubits) → AngleEmbedding → StronglyEntanglingLayers → probs → cosine kernel
- Integration: Sequential (quantum loss augments classical training)
- **IMPLEMENTED** — QuantumTripletLoss in loss/quantum_triplet_loss.py; feat_dim=None for lazy init (actual feat is 512-dim)

---
name: survey-postprocessing
description: Quantum post-processing techniques from survey paper — applied after classical model inference
metadata:
  type: project
---

Source: "Toward Quantum-Enhanced Computer Vision" (Connor Druett et al.)

## Techniques

### Quantum Annealing for Spatial Smoothing (MRF / Ising Model)
- After per-pixel classification: map probabilistic outputs to Markov Random Field / Ising model
- Classifier confidence → local bias; spatial pixel relationships → coupling strengths
- D-Wave finds ground state = globally consistent label assignment; reduces noise/inconsistency
- Result: significantly reduced noise and improved spatial continuity vs raw classical output [Gardas et al. 23]
- Application: hyperspectral image classification
- Integration: Sequential (classical classifier → quantum annealer)
- **Not in project**

### Quantum Probabilistic Label Refining (QPLR)
- VQC processes hard labels/logits from classical model; encodes into density matrix capturing inter-class correlations
- Measurement produces soft, correlation-aware labels with probabilistic distributions — richer than label smoothing
- Result: improved robustness against label noise and better calibration [Qi et al. 71]
- Promising for datasets with inherent class ambiguity or overlap (e.g., aerial/ground person re-ID)
- Integration: Sequential (classical model → QPLR post-processor)
- **Not in project** — potentially relevant given aerial/ground viewpoint ambiguity in AG-VPReID

### Hybrid Quantum GAN for Image Generation/Refinement (PQWGAN)
- Quantum sub-generators produce specific image patches; classical layers stitch + refine
- Avoids qubit limitation of full-image quantum generation; focuses quantum on patch-level generation
- Results: improved FID and higher Inception scores vs classical GAN with comparable params [Tsang et al. 84]; competitive FID + improved training stability [O'Dwyer Boyle & Nikandish 61]; 5-8 qubits per sub-generator
- Integration: Interlaced (quantum patch generators + classical refinement)
- **Not in project**

### Quantum K-Means Post-Processing for Segmentation
- After initial classification, quantum K-means (Schrödinger wave function cluster model) refines segmentation
- Separates non-convex cluster geometries more accurately than classical K-means
- Result: >99.6% accuracy, Dice > 0.85 [Poggiali et al. 68]; theoretically faster than classical
- Integration: Sequential (classical classifier → quantum K-means refinement)
- **Not in project**

### Quantum Swap Test Reranking — project-specific
- Computes quantum fidelity |⟨q|g⟩|² between query and top-K gallery candidates via CSWAP circuit
- Reranks classical L2 top-K by quantum overlap metric; O(K) circuit calls per query
- Result: -20.4pp Rank-1 vs classical L2 (45.5% vs 58.1%); quantum overlap metric on random projection to 4 qubits scrambles 2048-dim feature geometry — same concentration problem as IQP kernel
- n_qubits=8 too slow (>50 min); n_qubits=4 ran in ~72 min for 2528 queries
- Integration: Sequential (classical ranking → quantum reranking)
- **IMPLEMENTED** — utils/quantum_retrieval.py QuantumSwapTestRanker; post-processing quantum retrieval doesn't work with this approach

### Dürr-Høyer Quantum Minimum Finding — project-specific
- O(√N) oracle calls quantum minimum finding; directly finds nearest-neighbour in gallery
- DH result placed at top; rest filled from classical L2 order
- Provides theoretical speedup; accuracy should match classical (finds same minimum)
- Pending rerun after import math fix
- Integration: Sequential (replaces classical nearest-neighbour search)
- **IMPLEMENTED** — utils/quantum_retrieval.py DurrHoyerSearch

### Classical Noise Mitigation (Zero Noise Extrapolation, Virtual Distillation)
- ZNE: intentionally scales up noise, extrapolates to zero-noise limit
- Virtual Distillation: multiple copies of quantum state remove incoherent errors
- Required for any quantum component on real hardware (NISQ era)
- Integration: Cross-cutting — applied after any quantum circuit execution
- **Not in project** (relevant for future hardware deployment of existing components)

**Model Builder Files** (instantiate quantum architectures):

  - Examples: `make_model_qtemporal.py`, `make_model_qfc.py`, `make_model_qgated.py`, etc.
  - All follow the same pattern: load classical ViT-B-16, insert quantum module(s), return model

---

### 2. QUANTUM TEMPORAL GATED (QGT) — FULL IMPLEMENTATION

**File**: `/home/ubuntu/TF-CLIP-quantum/quantum_models/angle/quantum_temporal_gated.py`

**Architecture** (lines 9-26):
```
Input x: [B, T, in_features]
1. mean_feat = x.mean(1)                                  [B, in_features]
2. pre_net: Linear(in_features → n_qubits, bias=False)   per frame
3. sigmoid(·) * π                                         angles ∈ (0, π)
4. VQC (T frames, shared weights):
      for t in range(T):
          AngleEmbedding + StronglyEntanglingLayers
   → probs [B, 2^n_qubits]
5. upscale: Linear(2^n_qubits → in_features, bias=False) → delta [B, in_features]
6. gate_net: Linear(in_features → 1, bias=True) + sigmoid → g ∈ (0,1)
7. output = mean_feat + g * delta
```

**Key Design Details**:
- Gate initialized near 0.12 (bias=-2.0 → sigmoid(-2)≈0.12)
- Gate interpretation: g≈0 trusts mean-pool, g≈1 applies full VQC correction
- Stores `.last_gates` for per-sample analysis (which tracklets benefit from quantum)
- Bypass mode (`bypass_quantum=True`): returns plain `x.mean(1)`

**Weight Initialization** (lines 105-111):
```python
pre_net.weight:      kaiming_normal (fan_in)  — gradient preservation
qlayer_weights:      normal(0, 0.01)         — near-identity (avoid barren plateau)
upscale.weight:      normal(0, 0.001)        — residual delta ≈ 0 at init
gate_net.weight:     normal(0, 0.01)
gate_net.bias:       constant(-2.0)          — gate starts "closed" (low signal)
```

**Device Handling** (lines 113-118):
- VQC runs on CPU via `_apply()` override
- All tensors cast to float32 before circuit, back to input dtype after
- Handles both float16 and float32 inputs

**Shape Flow**:
```
Input:        [B, T, D=768]
mean_feat:    [B, 768]
angles:       [B, T, n_q=8]
q_out:        [B, 2^8=256]
delta:        [B, 768]
output:       [B, 768]
```

---

### 3. QUANTUM FRAME CORRELATION (QFC) — FULL IMPLEMENTATION

**File**: `/home/ubuntu/TF-CLIP-quantum/quantum_models/angle/quantum_frame_correlation.py`

**Architecture** (lines 9-26):
```
Input x: [B, T, in_features]
1. Build all pairs: T(T-1)/2 = 28 pairs for T=8 (or 6 for T=4)
   pair_feats: [B, n_pairs, 2*in_features]
2. pre_net: Linear(2*in_features → n_qubits, bias=False)   per pair
3. sigmoid(·) * π                                           → angles ∈ (0, π)
4. VQC (batched): all B*n_pairs through circuit at once
   → probs [B*n_pairs, 2^n_qubits]
5. Reshape & average over pairs:  [B, n_pairs, 2^n_q] → [B, 2^n_q]
6. upscale: Linear(2^n_qubits → in_features, bias=False)   → delta
7. output = mean_pool(x) + delta
```

**Key Innovation**:
- Only VQC variant that explicitly captures **cross-frame quantum interference**
- All T(T-1)/2 pair indices precomputed as buffers (`pair_i`, `pair_j`)
- Uses `qml.qnn.TorchLayer` (high-level wrapper) vs custom `@qml.qnode` decorator
- `TorchLayer` automatically broadcasts batch dimension through the circuit

**Shape Flow**:
```
Input:         [B, T=8, D=768]
n_pairs:       8*7/2 = 28
frames_i:      [B, 28, 768]
frames_j:      [B, 28, 768]
pair_feats:    [B, 28, 1536]
angles:        [B*28, 8] after reshape
q_out:         [B*28, 256] from circuit
averaged:      [B, 256] after reshape & mean(1)
delta:         [B, 768]
output:        [B, 768]
```

**Device Handling** (lines 113-118):
- `qlayer` pinned to CPU via custom `to()` override
- Input-device GPU→CPU transfer inside `forward()`

---

### 4. QUANTUM TEMPORAL AGGREGATION (TQA) — FIRST 120 LINES

**File**: `/home/ubuntu/TF-CLIP-quantum/quantum_models/angle/quantum_temporal.py`

**Architecture** (lines 9-25):
```
Input x: [B, T, in_features]
1. pre_net: Linear(in_features → n_qubits, bias=False)   per frame
2. sigmoid(·) * π                                         → angles ∈ (0, π)
3. VQC (T sequential uploads, shared weights):
      for t in range(T):
          AngleEmbedding(angles[t], rotation='Y')
          StronglyEntanglingLayers(weights)   # shared weights
   → probs() [2^n_qubits]
4. upscale: Linear(2^n_qubits → in_features, bias=False)
5. Skip: output = mean_pool(x) + delta
```

**Data Re-uploading Pattern** (lines 82-90):
- Circuit takes `[T, B, n_q]` angles (one row per frame)
- PennyLane broadcasts automatically over the B dimension
- Shared weights across all T uploads (e.g., shape `[2, 8, 3]` for n_layers=2, n_qubits=8)

**Initialization** (lines 104-108):
```python
pre_net:          kaiming_normal (fan_in)
qlayer_weights:   normal(0, 0.01)        # near-identity
upscale:          normal(0, 0.001)       # residual delta ≈ 0
```

**Key Difference from QGT**:
- TQA: no gate mechanism; always `output = mean_pool + delta`
- QGT: gate scales the delta contribution per sample

### 6. LOSS FUNCTION ARCHITECTURE (loss/make_loss.py)

**File**: `/home/ubuntu/TF-CLIP-quantum/loss/make_loss.py`

**Main Loss Composition** (lines 38-90):
```python
def loss_func(score, feat, target, target_cam, i2tscore=None, isprint=False):
    # score:     [B, num_classes] — classifier output
    # feat:      [B, 768] — feature vector(s) for triplet
    # target:    [B] — identity labels
    # i2tscore:  [B, num_classes] — CLIP I2T contrastive logits (optional)

    # ID Loss (softmax/cross-entropy)
    ID_LOSS = xent(score, target) if cfg.IF_LABELSMOOTH else CrossEntropyLoss(score, target)

    # Triplet Loss (metric learning)
    TRI_LOSS = triplet(feat, target)[0]
    # triplet(feat, target) returns (loss, _, _, _) — unpack first element

    # Combined Loss
    loss = cfg.ID_LOSS_WEIGHT * ID_LOSS + cfg.TRIPLET_LOSS_WEIGHT * TRI_LOSS

    # Optional: I2T contrastive loss (CLIP memory cache)
    if i2tscore is not None:
        I2TLOSS = xent(i2tscore, target)
        loss += cfg.I2T_LOSS_WEIGHT * I2TLOSS

    return loss
```

**Key Properties**:
- Supports **multiple classifier heads** as lists (e.g., primary + auxiliary)
- All heads use **same identity labels** (same target) — no per-head sampling
- **Triplet loss** operates on features, **ID loss** on classifier scores
- **I2T loss** is optional (requires CLIP text encoder stage 1)

**File**: `/home/ubuntu/TF-CLIP-quantum/utils/quantum_retrieval.py`

**A. Quantum Swap Test Reranker** (lines 49-151):

```python
class QuantumSwapTestRanker:
    # Per-pair circuit (1 ancilla + 2 registers of n_qubits each):
    # |0>_ancilla ⊗ query_state ⊗ gallery_state
    # H → CSWAP(ancilla, q_i, g_i) → H → measure
    # P(ancilla=0) = (1 + |<query|gallery>|²) / 2
    # similarity = 2*P(0) - 1 = |<query|gallery>|²
    
    # Top-K reranking workflow:
    # 1. Classical L2 search → top-50 candidates
    # 2. For each top-50 pair, run swap test
    # 3. Reorder by quantum similarity
    
    # Features: pre-projected to 2^n_qubits dims (random projection)
```

**B. Dürr–Høyer Quantum Minimum Finding** (lines 158-287):

```python
class DurrHoyerSearch:
    # Theoretical: O(√N) oracle calls on real quantum hardware
    # Simulator: classical oracle (precomputed L2), counts logical oracle calls
    # 
    # Workflow:
    # 1. Random initial best candidate
    # 2. Run Grover search for items closer than current best
    # 3. O(√N) total iterations → high probability of nearest neighbour
    #
    # Reports:
    # - oracle_calls_used (measured)
    # - theoretical_speedup = N / oracle_calls_used
    # - actual_sim_time (wall clock, not hardware-representative)
```

### 8. CIRCUIT STRUCTURE PATTERNS & PRE_NET/UPSCALE DESIGN

**Universal Pattern** (all VQC variants):
```
x [B, D]  OR  x [B, T, D]
    ↓
PRE_NET: Linear(D → n_qubits)
    • bias=False (no intercept)
    • weight init: kaiming_normal_(mode='fan_in', a=0)
    • output std ~ sqrt(2/D) ≈ 0.051 for D=768
    ↓
SCALING: sigmoid(·) * π  (NOT tanh)
    • Maps (-∞, +∞) → (0, π)
    • Critical: sigmoid(0)=0.5 maps to π/2 (max gradient of cos)
    • tanh(0)=0 maps to 0 (null gradient — bad for learning)
    ↓
QVIRTUALCIRCUIT:
    1. AngleEmbedding (rotation='Y'): RY(θ_i) per qubit
       – For dense_angle encoding: RY + RZ per qubit (2 features/qubit)
    2. StronglyEntanglingLayers (n_layers, n_qubits, 3):
       – Per layer: SU(2) Rot on each qubit + long-range CNOT entangling
       – weight shape: (n_layers, n_qubits, 3) → ~48 params for n_layers=2, n_qubits=8
    3. Measurement: qml.probs(wires=all) → 2^n_qubits amplitudes
    ↓
UPSCALE: Linear(2^n_qubits → D)
    • Near-zero init: normal_(0, std=0.001)
    • Residual connection: output = x + upscale(vqc_out)
    • At init: upscale_weight ≈ 0 → vqc_delta ≈ 0 → output ≈ x (classical baseline preserved)
```

**Why This Structure Works**:
1. **Residual skips prevent collapse**: Without residual, VQC-only outputs have no baseline. With skip, model starts as classical, learns to add quantum corrections.
2. **Near-zero upscale init ensures stability**: Prevents sudden performance drops at epoch 0.
3. **Sigmoid scaling preserves gradients**: tanh(0)=0 kills gradients; sigmoid(0)→π/2 keeps them.
4. **Strong entangling over basic**: BasicEntanglerLayers ≈ classical linear; StronglyEntanglingLayers creates actual multi-qubit correlations.

---

### 9. SHAPE FLOW THROUGH THE SYSTEM

**Complete Forward Path** (QTemporal example):

```
Input video batch:
  x [64, 8, 3, 256, 128]  (B=64, T=8, C=3, H=256, W=128)

ViT Image Encoder:
  Unfold to frames: [512, 3, 256, 128]  (B*T = 64*8)
  ↓
  ViT-B-16 forward:
    • Patchify: [512, 768, 197]  (197 = (256-16)/16 + 1, includes CLS)
    • Transformer blocks: [512, 768]
  ↓
  CLS token (position 0): [512, 768]

Reshape to tracklet:
  img_feature [64, 8, 768]  (back to [B, T, D])

QuantumTemporalAgg:
  Input: [64, 8, 768]
  ├─ pre_net(per frame): [64*8, 768] → [64*8, 8]
  ├─ angles: sigmoid([64, 8, 8]) * π → [64, 8, 8]
  ├─ VQC (T frames, B samples):
  │  Input to circuit: [8, 64, 8]  (T, B, n_q) for parameter broadcasting
  │  Output: [64, 256]  (B, 2^n_qubits)
  ├─ upscale: [64, 256] → [64, 768]
  └─ output: [64, 768] = mean([64, 8, 768]) + [64, 768]

Bottleneck (BN):
  [64, 768] → BN → [64, 768]

Classification:
  [64, 768] → linear(768→1604) → [64, 1604] logits

Loss Computation:
  scores [64, 1604]
  features [64, 768]  (for triplet)
  ID loss: CrossEntropyLoss(scores, labels)
  Triplet loss: HardTripletLoss(features, labels, margin=0.3)
  Total: ID_loss + triplet_loss + i2t_loss (optional)
```

### 11. INITIALIZATION PATTERNS & RESIDUAL STRATEGY

**All Quantum Modules Initialize Conservatively**:

| Component | Init Scheme | Std | Rationale |
|-----------|-----------|-----|-----------|
| `pre_net.weight` | kaiming_normal(fan_in) | ~0.05 | Preserve gradient flow, downstream sigmoid maps to π/2 |
| `qlayer.weights` | normal(0, 0.01) | 0.01 | Near-identity: minimal initial rotation between uploads |
| `upscale.weight` | normal(0, 0.001) | 0.001 | **Critical**: delta ≈ 0 at init, output ≈ identity |
| `gate_net.weight` | normal(0, 0.01) | 0.01 | Small perturbations around initialization |
| `gate_net.bias` | constant(-2.0) | — | Sigmoid(-2) ≈ 0.12 — gate starts "off" (trusts mean-pool) |

**Why Residuals Are Essential**:
```python
# WITHOUT residual: output = upscale(vqc(...))
# → At init, vqc_weights ≈ 0 → upscale outputs random noise ≈ N(0, σ²)
# → Loss jumps immediately, training destabilizes

# WITH residual: output = x + upscale(vqc(...))
# → At init, upscale(...) ≈ 0 → output ≈ x (classical baseline)
# → Loss starts low, model learns to apply small quantum corrections
# → Gradient flow preserved through skip connection
```

---

### 2. QUANTUM TEMPORAL GATED (QGT) — FULL IMPLEMENTATION

**File**: `/home/ubuntu/TF-CLIP-quantum/quantum_models/angle/quantum_temporal_gated.py`

**Architecture** (lines 9-26):
```
Input x: [B, T, in_features]
1. mean_feat = x.mean(1)                                  [B, in_features]
2. pre_net: Linear(in_features → n_qubits, bias=False)   per frame
3. sigmoid(·) * π                                         angles ∈ (0, π)
4. VQC (T frames, shared weights):

          AngleEmbedding + StronglyEntanglingLayers
   → probs [B, 2^n_qubits]
5. upscale: Linear(2^n_qubits → in_features, bias=False) → delta [B, in_features]
6. gate_net: Linear(in_features → 1, bias=True) + sigmoid → g ∈ (0,1)
7. output = mean_feat + g * delta
```

**Key Design Details**:
- Gate initialized near 0.12 (bias=-2.0 → sigmoid(-2)≈0.12)
- Gate interpretation: g≈0 trusts mean-pool, g≈1 applies full VQC correction
- Stores `.last_gates` for per-sample analysis (which tracklets benefit from quantum)
- Bypass mode (`bypass_quantum=True`): returns plain `x.mean(1)`


```python
def loss_func(score, feat, target, target_cam, i2tscore=None, isprint=False):
    # score:     [B, num_classes] — classifier output
    # feat:      [B, 768] — feature vector(s) for triplet
    # target:    [B] — identity labels
    # i2tscore:  [B, num_classes] — CLIP I2T contrastive logits (optional)

    # ID Loss (softmax/cross-entropy)
    ID_LOSS = xent(score, target) if cfg.IF_LABELSMOOTH else CrossEntropyLoss(score, target)

    # Triplet Loss (metric learning)
    TRI_LOSS = triplet(feat, target)[0]
    # triplet(feat, target) returns (loss, _, _, _) — unpack first element

    # Combined Loss
    loss = cfg.ID_LOSS_WEIGHT * ID_LOSS + cfg.TRIPLET_LOSS_WEIGHT * TRI_LOSS

    # Optional: I2T contrastive loss (CLIP memory cache)
    if i2tscore is not None:
        I2TLOSS = xent(i2tscore, target)
        loss += cfg.I2T_LOSS_WEIGHT * I2TLOSS

    return loss
```

**Key Properties**:
- Supports **multiple classifier heads** as lists (e.g., primary + auxiliary)
- All heads use **same identity labels** (same target) — no per-head sampling
- **Triplet loss** operates on features, **ID loss** on classifier scores

### 8. CIRCUIT STRUCTURE PATTERNS & PRE_NET/UPSCALE DESIGN

**Universal Pattern** (all VQC variants):
```
x [B, D]  OR  x [B, T, D]
    ↓
PRE_NET: Linear(D → n_qubits)
    • bias=False (no intercept)
    • weight init: kaiming_normal_(mode='fan_in', a=0)
    • output std ~ sqrt(2/D) ≈ 0.051 for D=768
    ↓
SCALING: sigmoid(·) * π  (NOT tanh)
    • Maps (-∞, +∞) → (0, π)
    • Critical: sigmoid(0)=0.5 maps to π/2 (max gradient of cos)
    • tanh(0)=0 maps to 0 (null gradient — bad for learning)
    ↓
QVIRTUALCIRCUIT:
    1. AngleEmbedding (rotation='Y'): RY(θ_i) per qubit
       – For dense_angle encoding: RY + RZ per qubit (2 features/qubit)
    2. StronglyEntanglingLayers (n_layers, n_qubits, 3):
       – Per layer: SU(2) Rot on each qubit + long-range CNOT entangling
       – weight shape: (n_layers, n_qubits, 3) → ~48 params for n_layers=2, n_qubits=8
    3. Measurement: qml.probs(wires=all) → 2^n_qubits amplitudes
    ↓
UPSCALE: Linear(2^n_qubits → D)
    • Near-zero init: normal_(0, std=0.001)
    • Residual connection: output = x + upscale(vqc_out)
    • At init: upscale_weight ≈ 0 → vqc_delta ≈ 0 → output ≈ x (classical baseline preserved)
```

**Why This Structure Works**:
1. **Residual skips prevent collapse**: Without residual, VQC-only outputs have no baseline. With skip, model starts as classical, learns to add quantum corrections.
2. **Near-zero upscale init ensures stability**: Prevents sudden performance drops at epoch 0.
3. **Sigmoid scaling preserves gradients**: tanh(0)=0 kills gradients; sigmoid(0)→π/2 keeps them.
4. **Strong entangling over basic**: BasicEntanglerLayers ≈ classical linear; StronglyEntanglingLayers creates actual multi-qubit correlations.

**Complete Forward Path** (QTemporal example):

```
Input video batch:
  x [64, 8, 3, 256, 128]  (B=64, T=8, C=3, H=256, W=128)

  Unfold to frames: [512, 3, 256, 128]  (B*T = 64*8)
  ↓
  ViT-B-16 forward:
    • Patchify: [512, 768, 197]  (197 = (256-16)/16 + 1, includes CLS)
    • Transformer blocks: [512, 768]
  ↓
  CLS token (position 0): [512, 768]

Reshape to tracklet:
  img_feature [64, 8, 768]  (back to [B, T, D])

QuantumTemporalAgg:
  Input: [64, 8, 768]
  ├─ pre_net(per frame): [64*8, 768] → [64*8, 8]
  ├─ angles: sigmoid([64, 8, 8]) * π → [64, 8, 8]
  ├─ VQC (T frames, B samples):
  │  Input to circuit: [8, 64, 8]  (T, B, n_q) for parameter broadcasting
  │  Output: [64, 256]  (B, 2^n_qubits)
  ├─ upscale: [64, 256] → [64, 768]
  └─ output: [64, 768] = mean([64, 8, 768]) + [64, 768]

Bottleneck (BN):
  [64, 768] → BN → [64, 768]

Classification:
  [64, 768] → linear(768→1604) → [64, 1604] logits

```

### 11. INITIALIZATION PATTERNS & RESIDUAL STRATEGY

**All Quantum Modules Initialize Conservatively**:

| Component | Init Scheme | Std | Rationale |
|-----------|-----------|-----|-----------|
| `pre_net.weight` | kaiming_normal(fan_in) | ~0.05 | Preserve gradient flow, downstream sigmoid maps to π/2 |
| `qlayer.weights` | normal(0, 0.01) | 0.01 | Near-identity: minimal initial rotation between uploads |
| `upscale.weight` | normal(0, 0.001) | 0.001 | **Critical**: delta ≈ 0 at init, output ≈ identity |
| `gate_net.weight` | normal(0, 0.01) | 0.01 | Small perturbations around initialization |
| `gate_net.bias` | constant(-2.0) | — | Sigmoid(-2) ≈ 0.12 — gate starts "off" (trusts mean-pool) |

**Why Residuals Are Essential**:
```python
# WITHOUT residual: output = upscale(vqc(...))
# → At init, vqc_weights ≈ 0 → upscale outputs random noise ≈ N(0, σ²)
# → Loss jumps immediately, training destabilizes

# WITH residual: output = x + upscale(vqc(...))
# → At init, upscale(...) ≈ 0 → output ≈ x (classical baseline)
# → Loss starts low, model learns to apply small quantum corrections
# → Gradient flow preserved through skip connection
```

```python
import pennylane as qml
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class MyQuantumModule(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, in_features, n_qubits=8, n_layers=2, device_name="default.qubit"):
        super().__init__()
        self.pre_net = nn.Linear(in_features, n_qubits, bias=False)
        
        dev = qml.device(device_name, wires=n_qubits)
        
        @qml.qnode(dev, interface="torch", diff_method="backprop")
        def _circuit(inputs, weights):
            qml.AngleEmbedding(inputs, wires=range(n_qubits), rotation="Y")
            qml.StronglyEntanglingLayers(weights, wires=range(n_qubits))
            return qml.probs(wires=range(n_qubits))
        
        self.qlayer = qml.qnn.TorchLayer(_circuit, {"weights": (n_layers, n_qubits, 3)})
        self.post_net = nn.Linear(2**n_qubits, output_dim, bias=False)
        self._init_weights()
    
    def _init_weights(self):
        nn.init.kaiming_normal_(self.pre_net.weight, a=0, mode="fan_in")
        nn.init.normal_(self.qlayer.weights, mean=0, std=0.01)  # near-identity
        nn.init.kaiming_uniform_(self.post_net.weight, a=math.sqrt(5))
    
    def to(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().to(*args, **kwargs)
        self.qlayer.to(device=torch.device("cpu"), dtype=torch.float32)  # pin to CPU
        return self
    
    def forward(self, x):
        input_dtype, input_device = x.dtype, x.device
        x = x.float()
        x = self.pre_net(x)
        x = torch.sigmoid(x) * math.pi
        x = x.cpu().float()
        x = self.qlayer(x)
        x = x.to(input_device)
        x = self.post_net(x)
        return x.to(input_dtype)
```

# Plan: Implement Remaining Survey Techniques + Deeper VQCs

## Context

The survey paper "Toward Quantum-Enhanced Computer Vision" (Connor Druett et al.) covers quantum techniques across five pipeline stages. Most are already implemented in TF-CLIP-quantum, but several remain. This plan maps every unimplemented technique to a concrete implementation, filtered by feasibility on our CPU PennyLane simulator (no D-Wave, no QPU). It also addresses the "lacking quantum parameters" problem — many VQC components have only ~48 trainable circuit weights drowned out by thousands of classical pre/post-net parameters.

---

## What Already Exists (Do NOT Reimplement)

| Technique | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| QHED | ✅ Implemented | preprocessing |
| QTemporal/TQA | ✅ Implemented | data re-uploading over T frames |
| QTD, QGT, QFC | ✅ Implemented | temporal variants |
| QClassifier (VQC head) | ✅ Implemented | quantum_layers.py QuantumClassifier |
| QClassifierReupload | ✅ Implemented (intractable) | 96-block, ~57s/batch — needs redesign |
| QuantumTripletLoss | ✅ Implemented | optimisation stage |
| QuantumSwapTest, DurrHoyer | ✅ Implemented | post-processing |
| Q-C-Q Interlaced | ✅ Implemented | quantum_interlaced.py |
| Parallel concat (PQCNN-style) | ✅ Implemented | quantum_feature_extractor.py |
| Dense Angle Encoding | ✅ In quantum_layers.py | NOT yet wired to temporal models |
| QChannel, QFrame, QGated, CCG | ✅ Implemented | adapter-style |

---

## Feasibility Filter

**Feasible on CPU PennyLane simulator (implement):**
Dense Angle Encoding wired to temporal models, QPLR, QuNN pre-ViT, QPCA simulation, light re-uploading (4–6 blocks), deeper VQC (n_layers=4), SPSA/COBYLA for circuit params

**Hardware-dependent (D-Wave / QPU) — simulation demo only:**
Quantum annealing for hyperparams, QAOA, Grover weight search, MRF/Ising annealing, PQWGAN

**Not applicable to re-ID pipeline:**
QFL (federated), QRL (reinforcement), Quantum K-means (unsupervised segmentation), PQWGAN (image generation)

---

## Implementation Plan

### STAGE 1 — Pre-processing

#### 1A. QuNN Patch Preprocessing (`quantum_models/angle/quantum_patch_embed.py`)
Quanvolutional layer applied to raw ViT patch embeddings before the transformer blocks. Each ViT patch embedding [B*T, 197, 768] passes through a shared VQC per patch, producing quantum-enhanced patch features that feed into ViT's positional embedding layer.

- New file: `quantum_models/angle/quantum_patch_embed.py`
  - Class `QuantumPatchEmbed(nn.Module)`
  - Input: `[B*T, N_patches, D=768]` → VQC per patch (shared weights) → same shape
  - Use `QuantumClassifier` from `quantum_layers.py` with output_dim=768 (residual)
  - Must integrate into `model/make_model_clipreid.py` before `image_encoder.blocks[0]`
- New file: `quantum_models/make_model_qpatch.py` — model builder
- New file: `train_qpatch.py` — training script
- **Key constraint**: 197 patches × B×T forward passes per batch — will be very slow. Start with n_qubits=4 and only apply to CLS token [B*T, 768] (not all patches) for tractability.
- Integration pattern: Sequential (quantum-first preprocessing) — runs at eval time

#### 1B. QPCA-Inspired Feature Compression (`quantum_models/angle/quantum_pca.py`)
Simulated quantum PCA: a VQC autoencoder that compresses 768-dim features to a quantum bottleneck and reconstructs. Not real QPCA (which needs phase estimation on QPU) but demonstrates the quantum compression principle with a reconstruction loss.

- New file: `quantum_models/angle/quantum_pca.py`
  - Class `QuantumAutoEncoder(nn.Module)`
  - Encoder: Linear(768→n_qubits) → VQC → probs [2^n_q]
  - Decoder: Linear(2^n_q → 768) (classical, no VQC in decoder — VQC is the bottleneck)
  - Reconstruction loss: MSE(decoded, input) added to training loss
  - The VQC bottleneck IS the quantum compression; probs vector is the compressed representation
- New file: `loss/quantum_recon_loss.py` — adds `recon_weight * MSE(decoded, original)` to total loss
- New file: `train_qpca.py` — training script with `--recon_weight` arg
- Integration: wraps around existing pooled features [B, 768], adds reconstruction signal

---

### STAGE 2 — Feature Extraction (Dense Angle + More Parameters)

#### 2A. Dense Angle Encoding for Temporal Models (`quantum_models/angle/quantum_temporal_dense.py`)
`dense_angle` mode already exists in `QuantumClassifier` (quantum_layers.py) but is not wired to `QTemporal`, `QTD`, or `QGT`. Dense angle encodes 2 features per qubit via RY + RZ rotation, doubling information density: n_qubits=8 can now encode 16 features instead of 8, directly addressing the 768→8 compression bottleneck documented in the survey.

- New file: `quantum_models/angle/quantum_temporal_dense.py`
  - Copy of `quantum_temporal.py` with circuit modified:
    ```python
    # Standard: AngleEmbedding(angles[:n_q], rotation='Y')  # n_q features used
    # Dense:    AngleEmbedding(angles[:n_q], rotation='Y')   # RY
    #           AngleEmbedding(angles[n_q:], rotation='Z')   # RZ — second n_q features
    # pre_net: Linear(D → 2*n_qubits) instead of Linear(D → n_qubits)
    ```
  - pre_net output: `2*n_qubits` (feeds both Y and Z rotations)
  - VQC circuit unchanged; `StronglyEntanglingLayers` on same n_qubits
  - Same residual pattern as QTemporal
- New file: `train_qtemporal_dense.py` — copy of `train_qtemporal.py`, uses `QuantumTemporalDense`
- **Why this matters**: Doubles the information the VQC receives without changing circuit depth or qubit count — no barren plateau increase, directly counters classical overshadowing

#### 2B. Deep VQC Temporal — n_layers=4 with Gradient Clipping (`quantum_models/angle/quantum_temporal_deep.py`)
Increasing n_layers from 2 to 4 doubles VQC circuit parameters (48→96). Risk of barren plateau mitigated by gradient norm clipping + near-identity initialization (std=0.005 instead of 0.01).

- New file: `quantum_models/angle/quantum_temporal_deep.py`
  - Identical to `quantum_temporal.py` except:
    - Default `n_layers=4`
    - `qlayer_weights` init std=0.005 (tighter near-identity)
    - Gradient clip is applied at the training-script level
- New file: `train_qtemporal_deep.py`
  - Add `--gradient_clip` flag (default 1.0)
  - `torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), args.gradient_clip)` in training loop
  - Monitors gradient norm per epoch (log if > threshold to detect barren plateau)

#### 2C. Light Re-uploading QTemporal — Independent Block Weights (`quantum_models/angle/quantum_temporal_reupload.py`)
QClassifierReupload (96 blocks, 57s/batch) is intractable. A 4-block re-uploading variant is feasible: ~4-6s/batch instead of 57s/batch. Crucially, each re-upload block gets **independent VQC weights** (unlike TQA which shares weights across all T uploads). This is closer to the survey's data re-uploading classifier which proved effective.

- New file: `quantum_models/angle/quantum_temporal_reupload.py`
  - Class `QuantumTemporalReupload(nn.Module)`
  - n_reupload=4 independent `StronglyEntanglingLayers` weight tensors
  - Each block: `AngleEmbedding(angles_t) → SEL_block_k → partial probs`
  - Aggregate: mean over n_reupload probs → upscale → residual
  - pre_net shared across all blocks (compression only); circuit weights independent
  - Total circuit params: n_reupload × n_layers × n_qubits × 3 = 4 × 2 × 8 × 3 = 192 (vs 48 for TQA)
- New file: `train_qtemporal_reupload.py`
  - `--n_reupload` arg (default 4, max 8 for tractability)

---

### STAGE 3 — Classification (More VQC Parameters)

#### 3A. Multi-Head VQC Classifier (`quantum_models/angle/quantum_multihead_classifier.py`)
Current QClassifier bottlenecks all 1604 classes through 2^8=256-dim VQC output. Multi-head approach: K independent VQC circuits, each classifying 1604/K classes. Final prediction is argmax over all heads. More quantum parameters (K × 48 circuit weights), avoids the single 256→1604 linear bottleneck.

- New file: `quantum_models/angle/quantum_multihead_classifier.py`
  - Class `QuantumMultiHeadClassifier(nn.Module)`
  - K=4 independent `QuantumClassifier` instances (from quantum_layers.py) each with `num_classes=1604`
  - Feature split: `Linear(768→768)` shared → K branches, each processes full 768 features
  - At inference: ensemble logits from K heads (sum or learned weighted sum)
  - Total VQC params: 4 × 48 = 192 vs 48 for single-head
- New file: `train_qmultihead.py`
  - `--n_heads` arg (default 4)

#### 3B. Deep QClassifier (n_layers=4, n_qubits=10)
n_qubits=10 gives 2^10=1024-dim output (vs 256 for n_qubits=8) — much richer representation for 1604 classes. Increase n_layers to 4 for more expressivity. The existing `QuantumClassifier` in `quantum_layers.py` supports this with just different hyperparameter args.

- No new file needed — modify `train_qclassifier.py` to add `--n_qubits 10 --n_layers 4`
- Modify `quantum_models/make_model_qclassifier.py` to pass these through
- Monitor barren plateau: log gradient norm per epoch

---

### STAGE 4 — Optimisation

#### 4A. SPSA Optimizer for Circuit Parameters (`utils/hybrid_optimizer.py`)
COBYLA and SPSA are more noise-robust than parameter-shift for deep circuits (survey finding from Friedrich & Maziero [21]). Implement a hybrid optimizer: Adam for classical (pre_net, upscale) params, SPSA for quantum circuit weights only. SPSA approximates gradient by simultaneous random perturbation of all params — independent of parameter count, important for larger re-uploading circuits.

- New file: `utils/hybrid_optimizer.py`
  - Class `SPSAOptimizer`
    - `__init__(params, lr=0.01, c=0.01, alpha=0.602, gamma=0.101)` — standard SPSA hyperparams
    - `step(closure)` — evaluates loss at two perturbations, estimates gradient direction
    - Identifies quantum params by `param.requires_grad and 'q_weights' in name`
  - Function `make_hybrid_optimizer(model, cfg)` — Adam for classical, SPSA for `.q_weights`
- New file: `train_qtemporal_spsa.py` — uses hybrid optimizer
- The `q_weights` naming convention is already consistent across all quantum modules

#### 4B. DQAS-Inspired Architecture Search (Circuit Structure Search)
Not full DQAS (too expensive), but a lightweight circuit structure ablation: systematically test which entanglement patterns (nearest-neighbour CNOT vs all-to-all vs Brickwork) in `StronglyEntanglingLayers` work best for temporal feature aggregation. Framed as architecture search.

- New file: `quantum_models/angle/quantum_temporal_configurable.py`
  - Adds `entanglement` arg: `'full'` (default SEL) | `'ring'` | `'linear'`
  - `'ring'`: CNOT(i, (i+1)%n_q) only — reduces gate depth, less prone to barren plateau on hardware
  - `'linear'`: CNOT(i, i+1) only — simplest, most hardware-friendly
  - Implements each via custom PennyLane circuit using `qml.CNOT` directly instead of SEL
- New file: `train_qtemporal_ent.py` — `--entanglement` arg for sweeping

---

### STAGE 5 — Post-processing

#### 5A. QPLR — Quantum Probabilistic Label Refining (`loss/quantum_label_refiner.py`)
The most novel unimplemented technique. After the classical classifier produces logits [B, 1604], a VQC processes the top-K class predictions and produces refined soft labels capturing inter-class correlations. Particularly valuable for AG-VPReID: aerial/ground pairs have inherent label ambiguity (same identity looks different across cameras). Standard cross-entropy treats all non-GT classes identically; QPLR captures quantum correlations between similar classes.

Architecture:
```
logits [B, 1604]
  → top-K selector → [B, K=32]          (work on top-32 classes only, tractable)
  → pre_net: Linear(K → n_qubits=8)
  → sigmoid·π → VQC → probs [B, 256]
  → refine_net: Linear(256 → K)          → quantum-refined logits for top-K
  → scatter back into full [B, 1604] logits (zero for non-top-K)
  → softmax → soft labels for cross-entropy loss
```

- New file: `loss/quantum_label_refiner.py`
  - Class `QuantumLabelRefiner(nn.Module)`
  - `forward(logits, target)` → `refined_loss` (KL divergence between refined soft labels and one-hot target)
  - Optional: `kl_weight` to blend with standard cross-entropy
  - Top-K selection is differentiable via straight-through estimator (or just use fixed top-K with no gradient through selector)
- Modify `loss/make_loss.py` to add `make_loss_qplr()` function
- New file: `train_qplr.py`
  - `--top_k_classes` arg (default 32, tractable)
  - `--kl_weight` arg (default 0.5)

#### 5B. Noise Mitigation Wrapper — Zero Noise Extrapolation (`utils/noise_mitigation.py`)
Required for any hardware deployment. On simulator it has no effect (no noise) but demonstrates readiness for real hardware. Implements ZNE: evaluate circuit at noise_factor ∈ {1, 3} and extrapolate to noise_factor=0.

- New file: `utils/noise_mitigation.py`
  - Function `zero_noise_extrapolation(circuit_fn, inputs, weights, noise_factors=[1,3])`
  - On `default.qubit` simulator: adds `qml.DepolarizingChannel` with scaled probability to mimic noise
  - Richardson extrapolation on probabilities
  - Wrapper class `ZNEWrappedCircuit` that replaces any `@qml.qnode` with ZNE-corrected version
- Add `--use_zne` flag to any eval script

---

### "More VQC Parameters" Summary Table

| Component | Current VQC params | Proposed fix | New VQC params |
|---|---|---|---|
| QTemporal (TQA) | 48 (2×8×3) | Dense angle encoding | 48 + richer input |
| QTemporal | 48 | n_layers=4 deep | 96 (4×8×3) |
| QTemporal | 48 | Light re-uploading 4 blocks | 192 (4×2×8×3) |
| QClassifier | 48 | n_qubits=10, n_layers=4 | 120 (4×10×3) |
| QClassifier | single head | Multi-head K=4 | 192 (4×48) |
| All VQCs | shared pre_net | Dense angle: pre_net(D→2n_q) | doubles input features used |

---

## Critical Files to Reference

- `quantum_models/angle/quantum_layers.py` — `QuantumClassifier`: base VQC block with dense_angle support; `to()` CPU-pinning pattern; weight init conventions
- `quantum_models/angle/quantum_temporal.py` — canonical temporal VQC pattern (copy and modify for new temporal variants)
- `quantum_models/angle/quantum_temporal_gated.py` — gate mechanism pattern for QPTemporal
- `quantum_models/angle/quantum_feature_extractor.py` — parallel concat pattern (already exists, reference for QPTemporal)
- `loss/make_loss.py` — how to add new loss variants (see `make_loss_q_triplet` at lines 101-182)
- `loss/quantum_triplet_loss.py` — VQC-in-loss pattern (QPLR follows same structure)
- `utils/quantum_retrieval.py` — circuit pattern for swap test (reference for ZNE wrapper)

---

## Recommended Build Order

1. **Dense angle encoding for temporal models** (2A) — smallest change, directly addresses documented bottleneck, ablation-ready
2. **QPLR** (5A) — novel post-processing contribution, relevant to aerial/ground ambiguity
3. **Light re-uploading temporal** (2C) — fixes the intractable QClassifierReupload with a feasible variant
4. **Deep VQC with gradient clipping** (2B) — tests barren plateau boundary systematically
5. **QPCA autoencoder** (1B) — quantum preprocessing demo with reconstruction loss
6. **SPSA hybrid optimizer** (4A) — alternative training signal for quantum params
7. **QuNN patch preprocessing** (1A) — run at eval time, most expensive, do last
8. **Multi-head classifier** (3A), Deep QClassifier (3B) — classification stage more VQC params
9. **DQAS structure search** (4B), ZNE noise mitigation (5B) — analysis/hardware-readiness

---

## Verification

For each new module:
1. Unit test: instantiate module, pass dummy `[4, 8, 768]` tensor, check output shape matches `[4, 768]`
2. 5-epoch smoke test: `SOLVER.STAGE2.MAX_EPOCHS 5 SOLVER.STAGE2.EVAL_PERIOD 999`

# Plan: Implement Remaining Survey Techniques + Deeper VQCs

## Context

The survey paper "Toward Quantum-Enhanced Computer Vision" (Connor Druett et al.) covers quantum techniques across five pipeline stages. Most are already implemented in TF-CLIP-quantum, but several remain. This plan maps every unimplemented technique to a concrete implementation, filtered by feasibility on our CPU PennyLane simulator (no D-Wave, no QPU). It also addresses the "lacking quantum parameters" problem — many VQC components have only ~48 trainable circuit weights drowned out by thousands of classical pre/post-net parameters.

Pipeline placement follows the survey's taxonomy strictly:
- **Pre-processing**: raw image operations before ViT backbone
- **Feature Extraction**: how features are learned (backbone-level, temporal pooling)
- **Classification**: decision head
- **Optimisation**: training-time changes
- **Post-processing**: after inference/retrieval

---

## What Already Exists (Do NOT Reimplement)

| Technique | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| QHED | ✅ Pre-processing | raw image edge detection before ViT |
| QTemporal/TQA | ✅ Feature Extraction | data re-uploading over T frames |
| QTD, QGT, QFC | ✅ Feature Extraction | temporal variants |
| QClassifier (VQC head) | ✅ Classification | quantum_layers.py QuantumClassifier |
| QClassifierReupload | ✅ Classification (intractable) | 96-block ~57s/batch — needs redesign |
| QuantumTripletLoss | ✅ Optimisation | kernel metric learning at train time |
| QuantumSwapTest, DurrHoyer | ✅ Post-processing | reranking after retrieval |
| Q-C-Q Interlaced | ✅ Feature Extraction | quantum_interlaced.py |
| Parallel concat (PQCNN-style) | ✅ Feature Extraction | quantum_feature_extractor.py |
| Dense Angle Encoding | ✅ In quantum_layers.py | NOT yet wired to temporal models |
| QChannel, QFrame, QGated, CCG | ✅ Feature Extraction | adapter-style |

---

## Feasibility Filter

**Feasible on CPU PennyLane simulator (implement these):**
Dense angle encoding for temporal models, QPLR, QPCA preprocessing simulation, QuNN-style patch processing, light re-uploading (4–6 blocks), deeper VQC (n_layers=4), SPSA/COBYLA for circuit params

**Hardware-dependent (D-Wave / QPU) — simulation demo only, lower priority:**
Quantum annealing for hyperparams (QAOA), Grover weight search, MRF/Ising annealing

**Not applicable to re-ID:**
QFL (federated), QRL (reinforcement learning), Quantum K-means (unsupervised segmentation), PQWGAN (image generation)

---

## Implementation Plan

### STAGE 1 — Pre-processing (raw image → ViT)

#### 1A. QPCA-Style Quantum Preprocessing (`quantum_models/angle/quantum_pca_preprocess.py`)
In the survey, QPCA is a preprocessing transform on raw image data before the backbone. In our system, raw image data enters as per-patch pixel tensors before ViT's patch embedding. We can't implement real QPCA (requires quantum phase estimation on QPU), but we can implement a **VQC-based channel-wise attention on raw input images** that learns a quantum-enhanced colour/texture filter — the quantum analogue of classical PCA whitening.

Architecture:
```
input image [B*T, C=3, H=256, W=128]
  → global avg pool → [B*T, 3]           (channel descriptor)
  → pre_net: Linear(3 → n_qubits=4)      (3 channels → 4 qubits; small is fast)
  → sigmoid·π → VQC → probs [B*T, 16]   (2^4=16)
  → channel_weights: Linear(16 → 3) + sigmoid  → [B*T, 3] ∈ (0,1)
  → output = input * channel_weights[:, :, None, None]  (channel rescaling)
```

This runs on raw images (pre-processing stage), shapes ViT's input by quantum-learned channel emphasis, is fast (only 3 channels, n_qubits=4), and runs at BOTH train and eval time (unlike adapter-style modules).

- New file: `quantum_models/angle/quantum_pca_preprocess.py`
  - Class `QuantumChannelPreprocess(nn.Module)`
  - Integration point: in `model/make_model_clipreid.py` forward, apply before `image_encoder(img)`
  - Multiplicative residual: `output = image * (1 + channel_weights)` (init to identity)
  - channel_weights linear bias init = 0.0 → sigmoid(0)=0.5 → rescale by 1.5 at init; adjust so init ≈ identity: bias = -4 → sigmoid(-4) ≈ 0.018 → output ≈ input × 1.018 ≈ identity
- New file: `quantum_models/make_model_qpca_pre.py`
- New file: `train_qpca_pre.py`
- Integration pattern: Sequential (quantum-first preprocessing, runs at eval)

#### 1B. QPIE-Style Quantum Image Encoding Filter (`quantum_models/angle/quantum_pie_preprocess.py`)
QPIE encodes pixel intensities as probability amplitudes. In simulation, this means treating each image patch as a quantum state vector and applying a learned unitary rotation. Implementation: apply VQC to each spatial grid cell of the feature map after first conv/patch op.

Practical approach: apply a tiny 2-qubit VQC per 2×2 spatial block on the 3-channel input, producing a quantum-filtered image at the same resolution.

- This is architecturally identical to 1A but applied spatially (per spatial block, not per channel)
- More expensive than 1A but more faithful to QPIE
- New file: `quantum_models/angle/quantum_pie_preprocess.py`
  - Class `QuantumSpatialFilter(nn.Module)`: splits image into 4×4 non-overlapping spatial patches, applies shared 2-qubit VQC to each patch, reassembles
  - n_qubits=2 (very fast: 2^2=4 states), shared weights across all spatial positions
- New file: `train_qpie_pre.py`

---

### STAGE 2 — Feature Extraction

#### 2A. QuNN-Style Temporal Feature Extractor (`quantum_models/angle/quantum_temporal_dense.py`)
In the survey, QuNNs apply quantum circuits as convolutional filters to produce feature maps. In our ViT system, the equivalent is a quantum circuit applied to the per-frame ViT features [B, T, 768] — which is exactly what the existing temporal models do. The survey distinction between "QuNN" and our temporal VQCs is mostly architectural framing; what's genuinely new is **dense angle encoding** which is the information-density improvement that makes QuNNs more expressive: encode 2 features per qubit (RY + RZ), doubling input capacity without more qubits.

Dense angle encoding already exists in `QuantumClassifier` (`quantum_layers.py`) but is NOT wired to the temporal models. Wire it now.

New circuit vs standard:
```python
# Standard AngleEmbedding (1 feature/qubit):
qml.AngleEmbedding(angles[:, :n_q], wires=range(n_q), rotation='Y')
# Dense (2 features/qubit):
qml.AngleEmbedding(angles[:, :n_q], wires=range(n_q), rotation='Y')   # RY
qml.AngleEmbedding(angles[:, n_q:], wires=range(n_q), rotation='Z')   # RZ
# pre_net output: Linear(D → 2*n_qubits) instead of Linear(D → n_qubits)
```

- New file: `quantum_models/angle/quantum_temporal_dense.py`
  - Class `QuantumTemporalDense(nn.Module)` — copy of `quantum_temporal.py` with dense encoding
  - `pre_net: Linear(in_features, 2*n_qubits)` — double the compressed output
  - Circuit adds second `AngleEmbedding(..., rotation='Z')` after first
  - Everything else (residual, upscale, init) identical
- New file: `train_qtemporal_dense.py`
- Apply same pattern to QTD: `quantum_temporal_diff_dense.py` + `train_qtd_dense.py`
- **Why this matters**: directly addresses 768→8 compression bottleneck documented in survey; same circuit depth, no barren plateau increase

#### 2B. Deep VQC Temporal — n_layers=4 with Gradient Clipping
More circuit parameters per block (48→96 weights). Near-identity init tightened to std=0.005. Barren plateau risk managed via gradient clipping at training time.

- New file: `quantum_models/angle/quantum_temporal_deep.py`
  - Identical to `quantum_temporal.py` with default `n_layers=4`, init std=0.005
- New file: `train_qtemporal_deep.py`
  - `--gradient_clip` flag (default 1.0)
  - Logs gradient norm per epoch for barren plateau detection: if grad_norm < 1e-4 flag warning

#### 2C. Light Re-uploading Temporal — Independent Block Weights (`quantum_models/angle/quantum_temporal_reupload.py`)
QClassifierReupload (96 blocks) is intractable (~57s/batch). 4-block variant: ~4–6s/batch. Crucially, each block uses **independent VQC weights** (unlike TQA which shares weights across all T frame uploads). This is the survey's data re-uploading classifier concept applied to temporal features.

- New file: `quantum_models/angle/quantum_temporal_reupload.py`
  - Class `QuantumTemporalReupload(nn.Module)`
  - `n_reupload` independent `StronglyEntanglingLayers` weight tensors (nn.ParameterList)
  - Each block: `AngleEmbedding(frame_angles_t) → SEL_k` — frame index t cycles modulo n_reupload
  - After all T frames: measure probs → upscale → residual
  - Total circuit params: n_reupload × n_layers × n_qubits × 3 = 4×2×8×3 = 192 (vs 48 for TQA)
- New file: `train_qtemporal_reupload.py` (`--n_reupload` arg, default 4)

#### 2D. QPCA Autoencoder on Extracted Features (`quantum_models/angle/quantum_autoencoder.py`)
After ViT extracts per-frame features [B, T, 768], a VQC autoencoder compresses and reconstructs them. This is "quantum autoencoder as feature extractor" from the survey. The VQC bottleneck IS the compressed representation; reconstruction loss forces it to preserve information. At inference, only the encoder path runs.

Architecture:
```
x [B, 768] → pre_net(768→n_q) → sigmoid·π → VQC → probs [2^n_q]  ← quantum bottleneck
           ↓                                                         ← reconstruct
           upscale(2^n_q→768)  → x_recon [B, 768]
Additional loss: MSE(x_recon, x.detach()) * recon_weight
```

- New file: `quantum_models/angle/quantum_autoencoder.py`
  - Class `QuantumAutoEncoder(nn.Module)` integrating into temporal pooling (operates on mean-pooled [B,768])
- New file: `loss/quantum_recon_loss.py` — `recon_weight * F.mse_loss(x_recon, x_original)` added to total loss
- New file: `train_qautoencoder.py` (`--recon_weight` arg, default 0.1)

---

### STAGE 3 — Classification

#### 3A. Multi-Head VQC Classifier (`quantum_models/angle/quantum_multihead_classifier.py`)
Current single-head QClassifier: 768→n_q→VQC→256→1604. Problem: single 256-dim VQC output is a severe bottleneck for 1604 classes. Multi-head: K=4 independent VQC heads, each producing 256-dim quantum features, concatenated to 1024-dim, then projected to 1604 classes. Total circuit params: 4×48=192.

- New file: `quantum_models/angle/quantum_multihead_classifier.py`
  - Class `QuantumMultiHeadClassifier(nn.Module)`
  - K `QuantumClassifier` instances (reuse from `quantum_layers.py`)
  - Each head: separate `pre_net(768→n_q)` + independent VQC weights
  - Concat outputs: `[B, K*256]` → `Linear(K*256, num_classes)`
  - `bypass_quantum=True`: replaces each head with `Linear(768→256)+ReLU`
- New file: `train_qmultihead.py` (`--n_heads` arg, default 4)

#### 3B. Deep QClassifier (n_qubits=10, n_layers=4)
n_qubits=10 → 2^10=1024-dim VQC output (vs 256 for n_qubits=8), much richer for 1604 classes. The existing `QuantumClassifier` in `quantum_layers.py` supports this with just hyperparameter changes.

- No new module file — modify `quantum_models/make_model_qclassifier.py` to accept `--n_qubits 10 --n_layers 4`
- Modify `train_qclassifier.py` to expose these args
- New training script `train_qclassifier_deep.py` with these as defaults + gradient clipping

---

### STAGE 4 — Optimisation

#### 4A. SPSA Hybrid Optimizer (`utils/hybrid_optimizer.py`)
Survey finding: SPSA and COBYLA are more noise-robust than parameter-shift for deep circuits. Hybrid: Adam for classical params (pre_net, upscale, gate_net), SPSA for quantum circuit weights only (`q_weights` / `qlayer.weights`). SPSA gradient estimate uses two forward passes with simultaneous random perturbation — cost independent of parameter count.

- New file: `utils/hybrid_optimizer.py`
  - Class `SPSAOptimizer(torch.optim.Optimizer)`
    - `__init__(params, lr=0.01, c=0.01, perturbation='rademacher')` — standard SPSA
    - `step(closure)`: two forward passes at (θ+c·Δ) and (θ-c·Δ), estimate gradient via finite diff
  - Function `make_hybrid_optimizer(model, cfg)`: splits model.parameters() by name — `'q_weights'` or `'qlayer.weights'` → SPSA; all others → Adam
- New file: `train_qtemporal_spsa.py` — uses hybrid optimizer
- `q_weights` naming is consistent across all quantum modules already

#### 4B. Entanglement Pattern Search (`quantum_models/angle/quantum_temporal_configurable.py`)
Lightweight version of DQAS: compare different entanglement topologies in StronglyEntanglingLayers. `'full'` (default) vs `'ring'` (nearest-neighbour only) vs `'linear'` (chain). Ring/linear are less expressive but more hardware-friendly and potentially less barren-plateau-prone.

- New file: `quantum_models/angle/quantum_temporal_configurable.py`
  - Class `QuantumTemporalConfigurable(nn.Module)`
  - `entanglement` arg: `'full'` | `'ring'` | `'linear'`
  - `'ring'` and `'linear'` implemented via explicit `qml.CNOT` loops replacing `StronglyEntanglingLayers`
- New file: `train_qtemporal_ent.py` (`--entanglement` arg for sweeping)

---

### STAGE 5 — Post-processing

#### 5A. QPLR — Quantum Probabilistic Label Refining (`loss/quantum_label_refiner.py`)
Most novel unimplemented technique. After the classifier produces logits [B, 1604], a VQC processes them to produce soft labels capturing inter-class quantum correlations. Particularly relevant for AG-VPReID: aerial/ground pairs create inherent class ambiguity (same identity looks different across cameras). Standard cross-entropy treats all wrong classes identically; QPLR learns quantum correlations between visually similar classes.

Architecture:
```
logits [B, 1604]
  → top-K selector (K=32) → [B, 32]          (top-32 class logits only; tractable)
  → pre_net: Linear(32 → n_qubits=8)
  → sigmoid·π → VQC → probs [B, 256]
  → refine_net: Linear(256 → 32) + softmax    → quantum-refined soft weights for top-32 classes
  → scatter back to full [B, 1604]             (non-top-32 get logit-proportional weight)
  → KL divergence against one-hot target
```

- New file: `loss/quantum_label_refiner.py`
  - Class `QuantumLabelRefiner(nn.Module)`
  - `forward(logits, target)` → `qplr_loss` (KL div)
  - `kl_weight` to blend with standard cross-entropy: `total = CE + kl_weight * KL`
  - Top-K selection is non-differentiable; use straight-through for gradients through selector
- Modify `loss/make_loss.py` to add `make_loss_qplr()` function
- New file: `train_qplr.py` (`--top_k_classes 32 --kl_weight 0.5`)

#### 5B. Zero Noise Extrapolation — ZNE (`utils/noise_mitigation.py`)
Required for hardware deployment. On `default.qubit` simulator it has no effect (no noise), but demonstrates readiness. Implements ZNE by intentionally adding `qml.DepolarizingChannel` noise at scaled levels and extrapolating to zero noise via Richardson extrapolation.

- New file: `utils/noise_mitigation.py`
  - Function `apply_zne(circuit_fn, inputs, weights, noise_factors=[1, 3], noise_prob=0.01)`
  - Evaluates circuit with DepolarizingChannel at each noise_factor, Richardson extrapolates
  - Wrapper class `ZNECircuit` wrapping any `@qml.qnode`
- Add `--use_zne` flag to eval scripts (eval_agvpreid_quantum.py)
- Useful when moving to hardware

---

## "More VQC Parameters" Summary

| Component | Current VQC params | Proposed | New VQC params |
|---|---|---|---|
| QTemporal (standard) | 48 (2×8×3) | Dense angle encoding | 48 params, but encodes 16 features (vs 8) |
| QTemporal | 48 | n_layers=4 deep | 96 (4×8×3) |
| QTemporal | 48 | Light re-uploading n=4 blocks | 192 (4×2×8×3) |
| QClassifier | 48 | n_qubits=10, n_layers=4 | 120 (4×10×3) |
| QClassifier | single head 48 | Multi-head K=4 | 192 (4×48) |

---

## Critical Files to Reference

- `quantum_models/angle/quantum_layers.py` — `QuantumClassifier` base VQC block (dense_angle already here); CPU-pinning pattern; init conventions
- `quantum_models/angle/quantum_temporal.py` — canonical temporal VQC pattern (copy-base for 2A, 2B, 2C)
- `quantum_models/angle/quantum_temporal_gated.py` — gate mechanism and `last_gates` pattern

- `loss/make_loss.py` — how to register new loss variants (see `make_loss_q_triplet` lines 101-182)

---

## Recommended Build Order

1. **Dense angle encoding temporal** (2A) — smallest change, directly addresses documented bottleneck
2. **QPLR** (5A) — novel post-processing contribution, aerial/ground ambiguity angle
3. **Light re-uploading** (2C) — fixes the intractable QClassifierReupload

#### 1A. QPCA-Style Quantum Preprocessing (`quantum_models/angle/quantum_pca_preprocess.py`)
In the survey, QPCA is a preprocessing transform on raw image data before the backbone. In our system, raw image data enters as per-patch pixel tensors before ViT's patch embedding. We can't implement real QPCA (requires quantum phase estimation on QPU), but we can implement a **VQC-based channel-wise attention on raw input images** that learns a quantum-enhanced colour/texture filter — the quantum analogue of classical PCA whitening.

Architecture:
```
input image [B*T, C=3, H=256, W=128]
  → global avg pool → [B*T, 3]           (channel descriptor)
  → pre_net: Linear(3 → n_qubits=4)      (3 channels → 4 qubits; small is fast)
  → sigmoid·π → VQC → probs [B*T, 16]   (2^4=16)
  → channel_weights: Linear(16 → 3) + sigmoid  → [B*T, 3] ∈ (0,1)
  → output = input * channel_weights[:, :, None, None]  (channel rescaling)
```

This runs on raw images (pre-processing stage), shapes ViT's input by quantum-learned channel emphasis, is fast (only 3 channels, n_qubits=4), and runs at BOTH train and eval time (unlike adapter-style modules).

- New file: `quantum_models/angle/quantum_pca_preprocess.py`
  - Class `QuantumChannelPreprocess(nn.Module)`
  - Integration point: in `model/make_model_clipreid.py` forward, apply before `image_encoder(img)`
  - Multiplicative residual: `output = image * (1 + channel_weights)` (init to identity)
  - channel_weights linear bias init = 0.0 → sigmoid(0)=0.5 → rescale by 1.5 at init; adjust so init ≈ identity: bias = -4 → sigmoid(-4) ≈ 0.018 → output ≈ input × 1.018 ≈ identity
- New file: `quantum_models/make_model_qpca_pre.py`
- New file: `train_qpca_pre.py`
- Integration pattern: Sequential (quantum-first preprocessing, runs at eval)

#### 1B. QPIE-Style Quantum Image Encoding Filter (`quantum_models/angle/quantum_pie_preprocess.py`)
QPIE encodes pixel intensities as probability amplitudes. In simulation, this means treating each image patch as a quantum state vector and applying a learned unitary rotation. Implementation: apply VQC to each spatial grid cell of the feature map after first conv/patch op.

Practical approach: apply a tiny 2-qubit VQC per 2×2 spatial block on the 3-channel input, producing a quantum-filtered image at the same resolution.

- This is architecturally identical to 1A but applied spatially (per spatial block, not per channel)
- More expensive than 1A but more faithful to QPIE
- New file: `quantum_models/angle/quantum_pie_preprocess.py`
  - Class `QuantumSpatialFilter(nn.Module)`: splits image into 4×4 non-overlapping spatial patches, applies shared 2-qubit VQC to each patch, reassembles
  - n_qubits=2 (very fast: 2^2=4 states), shared weights across all spatial positions
- New file: `train_qpie_pre.py`

### STAGE 2 — Feature Extraction

#### 2A. QuNN-Style Temporal Feature Extractor (`quantum_models/angle/quantum_temporal_dense.py`)
In the survey, QuNNs apply quantum circuits as convolutional filters to produce feature maps. In our ViT system, the equivalent is a quantum circuit applied to the per-frame ViT features [B, T, 768] — which is exactly what the existing temporal models do. The survey distinction between "QuNN" and our temporal VQCs is mostly architectural framing; what's genuinely new is **dense angle encoding** which is the information-density improvement that makes QuNNs more expressive: encode 2 features per qubit (RY + RZ), doubling input capacity without more qubits.

Dense angle encoding already exists in `QuantumClassifier` (`quantum_layers.py`) but is NOT wired to the temporal models. Wire it now.

New circuit vs standard:
```python
# Standard AngleEmbedding (1 feature/qubit):
qml.AngleEmbedding(angles[:, :n_q], wires=range(n_q), rotation='Y')
# Dense (2 features/qubit):
qml.AngleEmbedding(angles[:, :n_q], wires=range(n_q), rotation='Y')   # RY
qml.AngleEmbedding(angles[:, n_q:], wires=range(n_q), rotation='Z')   # RZ
# pre_net output: Linear(D → 2*n_qubits) instead of Linear(D → n_qubits)
```

- New file: `quantum_models/angle/quantum_temporal_dense.py`
  - Class `QuantumTemporalDense(nn.Module)` — copy of `quantum_temporal.py` with dense encoding
  - `pre_net: Linear(in_features, 2*n_qubits)` — double the compressed output
  - Circuit adds second `AngleEmbedding(..., rotation='Z')` after first
  - Everything else (residual, upscale, init) identical
- New file: `train_qtemporal_dense.py`
- Apply same pattern to QTD: `quantum_temporal_diff_dense.py` + `train_qtd_dense.py`
- **Why this matters**: directly addresses 768→8 compression bottleneck documented in survey; same circuit depth, no barren plateau increase

#### 2B. Deep VQC Temporal — n_layers=4 with Gradient Clipping
More circuit parameters per block (48→96 weights). Near-identity init tightened to std=0.005. Barren plateau risk managed via gradient clipping at training time.

- New file: `quantum_models/angle/quantum_temporal_deep.py`
  - Identical to `quantum_temporal.py` with default `n_layers=4`, init std=0.005
- New file: `train_qtemporal_deep.py`
  - `--gradient_clip` flag (default 1.0)
  - Logs gradient norm per epoch for barren plateau detection: if grad_norm < 1e-4 flag warning

#### 2C. Light Re-uploading Temporal — Independent Block Weights (`quantum_models/angle/quantum_temporal_reupload.py`)
QClassifierReupload (96 blocks) is intractable (~57s/batch). 4-block variant: ~4–6s/batch. Crucially, each block uses **independent VQC weights** (unlike TQA which shares weights across all T frame uploads). This is the survey's data re-uploading classifier concept applied to temporal features.

- New file: `quantum_models/angle/quantum_temporal_reupload.py`
  - Class `QuantumTemporalReupload(nn.Module)`
  - `n_reupload` independent `StronglyEntanglingLayers` weight tensors (nn.ParameterList)
  - Each block: `AngleEmbedding(frame_angles_t) → SEL_k` — frame index t cycles modulo n_reupload
  - After all T frames: measure probs → upscale → residual
  - Total circuit params: n_reupload × n_layers × n_qubits × 3 = 4×2×8×3 = 192 (vs 48 for TQA)
- New file: `train_qtemporal_reupload.py` (`--n_reupload` arg, default 4)

#### 2D. QPCA Autoencoder on Extracted Features (`quantum_models/angle/quantum_autoencoder.py`)
After ViT extracts per-frame features [B, T, 768], a VQC autoencoder compresses and reconstructs them. This is "quantum autoencoder as feature extractor" from the survey. The VQC bottleneck IS the compressed representation; reconstruction loss forces it to preserve information. At inference, only the encoder path runs.

Architecture:
```
x [B, 768] → pre_net(768→n_q) → sigmoid·π → VQC → probs [2^n_q]  ← quantum bottleneck
           ↓                                                         ← reconstruct
           upscale(2^n_q→768)  → x_recon [B, 768]
Additional loss: MSE(x_recon, x.detach()) * recon_weight
```

- New file: `quantum_models/angle/quantum_autoencoder.py`
  - Class `QuantumAutoEncoder(nn.Module)` integrating into temporal pooling (operates on mean-pooled [B,768])
- New file: `loss/quantum_recon_loss.py` — `recon_weight * F.mse_loss(x_recon, x_original)` added to total loss
- New file: `train_qautoencoder.py` (`--recon_weight` arg, default 0.1)

### STAGE 3 — Classification

#### 3A. Multi-Head VQC Classifier (`quantum_models/angle/quantum_multihead_classifier.py`)
Current single-head QClassifier: 768→n_q→VQC→256→1604. Problem: single 256-dim VQC output is a severe bottleneck for 1604 classes. Multi-head: K=4 independent VQC heads, each producing 256-dim quantum features, concatenated to 1024-dim, then projected to 1604 classes. Total circuit params: 4×48=192.

- New file: `quantum_models/angle/quantum_multihead_classifier.py`
